sessions.name: handshake-and-initial-set
sessions.description: Hello and Welcome, then every column kind in one initial set: the set spans several chunks, so chunk 0 carries the descriptor and later chunks carry null. Rows 1-4 are SampleRows variants 0-3, so every value here is one the module wrote. A second subscription matches nothing: an empty set still carries its descriptor and its anchor.

CallReducer 1: PutSample({"tag":"Int64","value":"1"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"0"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"1"}).
CallReducer 2: PutSample({"tag":"Int64","value":"2"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"1"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"1"}).
CallReducer 3: PutSample({"tag":"Int64","value":"3"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"2"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"1"}).
CallReducer 4: PutSample({"tag":"Int64","value":"4"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"3"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"1"}).
Subscribe 1: SELECT * FROM Sample WHERE Group = :g (:g = 1).
Subscribe 2: SELECT * FROM Sample WHERE Group = :g (:g = 99).

sessions.name: deltas
sessions.description: Inserts, updates, and deletes as TransactionUpdate frames. Subscriptions 1 (Group 10-20) and 2 (Group = 20) overlap, so a row in both arrives once per subscription in one frame. Subscription 1 is then re-scoped to 21-30: the diff arrives as a TransactionUpdate at LSN 0, which a client applies without judging it against the anchor. Finally an unsubscribe.

steps.send: Hello offering protocol versions 2-3 with a bearer token.
Subscribe 1: SELECT * FROM Sample WHERE Group BETWEEN :lo AND :hi (:lo = 10, :hi = 20).
Subscribe 2: SELECT * FROM Sample WHERE Group = :g (:g = 20).
CallReducer 1: PutSample({"tag":"Int64","value":"10"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"0"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"10"}).
CallReducer 2: PutSample({"tag":"Int64","value":"20"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"2"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"20"}).
CallReducer 3: ChangeSample({"tag":"Int64","value":"20"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"1"}).
CallReducer 4: DeleteSample({"tag":"Int64","value":"10"}).
CallReducer 5: PutSample({"tag":"Int64","value":"25"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"0"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"25"}).
Re-scope subscription 1 to Group 21-30: row 20 leaves, row 25 enters.
Unsubscribe 2.

sessions.name: call-and-subscribe-failures
sessions.description: A reducer that rejects, an unknown reducer, wrong arguments, and subscriptions the server refuses. Call failures are ReducerResult frames with ok=false; a refused subscription is an Error frame carrying its subscription id.

sessions.name: column-masks
sessions.description: A column policy hides Secret.Hidden from everyone but the row's owner. The caller's own row arrives with an empty mask (every column present); another identity's row arrives with a mask, and its row bytes simply do not contain the hidden column. Keys here are string-encoded.

sessions.name: producers
sessions.description: Producer calls (protocol 3). The result is one tagged value in the reducer-argument encoding: a record is an Array of its fields in declaration order, a list an Array of its elements. A trailing parameter with a default may be left off.

CallReducer 2: PutSample({"tag":"Int64","value":"51"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"2"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"50"}).

CallProducer 4: Summarize({"tag":"Int64","value":"98"}).
CallProducer 5: NoSuchProducer().

sessions.name: heartbeat
sessions.description: The client pings and the server answers with the same id; then the server's heartbeat fires (the run moves the server's clock) and the client must answer the server's Ping with a Pong, or be disconnected after Transport:HeartbeatTimeoutMs.

steps.send: Hello offering protocol versions 2-3 with a bearer token.
Client sends Ping 7.
The server's clock moves 60000 ms: its heartbeat sends a Ping.

sessions.name: resume-before-drop
sessions.description: A subscription receives one delta, then the socket drops without a close. The client's resume cursor is the highest LSN it fully applied: the LSN of that TransactionUpdate.

steps.send: Hello offering protocol versions 2-3 with a bearer token.
Subscribe 1: SELECT * FROM Sample WHERE Group = :g (:g = 40).
CallReducer 1: PutSample({"tag":"Int64","value":"40"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"0"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"40"}).

sessions.name: resume-gap-writer
sessions.description: While the first client is away, another connection commits a row its subscription matches.

steps.send: Hello offering protocol versions 2-3 with a bearer token.
CallReducer 1: PutSample({"tag":"Int64","value":"41"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"2"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"40"}).

sessions.name: resume-accepted
sessions.description: The client reconnects and sends Resume with the epoch from its old Welcome, its cursor, and its subscriptions (same ids, queries, parameters). The server accepts and replays the gap as ordinary TransactionUpdate frames; the client keeps the descriptor it already held, so no initial set and no descriptor arrive. The subscription then carries on live.

steps.send: Hello offering protocol versions 2-3 with a bearer token.
Resume against the original epoch from the cursor; subscription 1 as before. Rows decode against the descriptor held from session resume-before-drop.
CallReducer 1: PutSample({"tag":"Int64","value":"42"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"0"}, {"tag":"Int64","value":"40"}).

sessions.name: resume-rejected
sessions.description: A Resume against an epoch this server's log is not: rejected. The client must discard every cached row and re-establish each subscription with an ordinary Subscribe, which answers with a full initial set.

steps.send: Hello offering protocol versions 2-3 with a bearer token.
Resume against an epoch the server never had.

expect.reason: Unknown or stale log epoch; a full resync is required.

sessions.name: reauthenticate
sessions.description: A fresh token for the same identity is accepted. A token for a different identity is not a refresh: the server sends identity_changed and closes the connection.

steps.send: Hello offering protocol versions 2-3 with a bearer token.
Reauthenticate with a fresh token for the same subject.
Reauthenticate with a token for a different subject.

expect.message: Reauthenticate presented a token for a different identity; a connection is bound to one identity for its lifetime. Reconnect.
